newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas weakened by CGE cable TV unit - source.
newsitem.headline: Havas weakened by CGE cable TV unit - source.

text.p: The stake held by Agence Havas in Compagnie Generale des Eaux's (CGE) loss-making cable TV unit CGV could weigh more heavily than expected on 1997 results, a source close to the companies said on Monday.
Havas has a buy option on CGV up to end-October and may have to sell assets to achieve the profit growth it has forecast, the source said.
Havas will also suffer from losses at Generale d'Images, CGE's television production unit, which should be higher this year than last, another source said.

When Havas and CGE announced their accord, which through share and asset swaps makes CGE the biggest single shareholder in Havas and Havas the major shareholder in Canal Plus, CGE said it wanted to sell CGV (Compagnie Generale de Videocommumnication) this year to a partner chosen with Havas and Canal Plus.
It said at the time it was talking with various international companies which could be interested in CGV, including TCI Communications Inc and Time Warner Inc.
CGV, which at end-1995 was owned 71.6 percent by CGE and 20 percent by Canal Plus, would be recapitalised by CGE if Havas exercises its call option.

A Havas spokesman said the company was seeking a partner for CGV in conjunction with CGE and Canal Plus, and the consultation between the three firms over this should be completed by the end of September.
If there is no common choice for a partner by that date, the groups will have another month to define CGV's future, he said.
Analysts estimate CGV lost some 300 million francs in 1996.
Losses at Generale d'Images came to 100 million francs in 1996 and should increase in 1997, a source said.
Havas has said that, for 1997, the cost of Generale d'Images and its bigger stake in Canal Plus should be 150 million francs.
Havas is to increase its stake in Canal Plus from 23.6 percent to 34.4 percent after buying CGE's Canal Plus shares and following the fusion of Canal Plus with Nethold at the end of April.
This will increase Havas's share of the losses which are expected at Canal Plus following its merger with Nethold, a broadcasting share analyst said.
"... To smooth out its results, Havas will have to take plenty of exceptional items and carry out asset sales," said the analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Havas has forecast 1997 net attributable profit of 1.5 billion francs and aims to increase earnings per share by five percent in 1998.
It has said it would achieve this by "improving results in traditional sectors, reducing losses in audiovisual and from the impact of refocusing certain activities".
When Havas and CGE announced their accord on February 6, Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier, asked about disposals, said there would be "no list, no time scale and no amount".

Havas has already agreed to one disposal. At the end of February it and France Telecom each took buy and sell options for the whole of ODA, which handles all advertising carried in France Telecom's telephone directories and is valued at 2.5 billion francs.

Analysts say that would leave Comareg, Havas's free newspaper subsidiary, with an estimated value of 1.8 billion francs, and Havas Voyages, its travel agency, with an estimated value of 1.3 billion francs.
Havas is in the process of carrying out an audit at Havas Voyages. It has said it is "obliged to think about a change in its (Havas Voyages') position".

However, Dauzier said in a newspaper interview published on Monday that Havas would remain the main shareholder in Havas Advertising, and that weekly news magazines Le Point and L'Express were not for sale.
